record.paper_title: Mini-Proceedings ECT* Workshop: Hadronic Atoms and Kaonic Nuclei
record.original_question: Can stopped antiproton annihilation in light nuclei produce deeply bound double-strange, S = −2, double-antikaon dibaryon systems such as K−K−pp, and can exclusive measurements of K+K0 missing mass and correlated ΛΛ decays establish such states with sufficient resolution and statistics?

evidence.quote: Recently antiproton annihilation in nuclei was proposed to search for deeply bound double-strange systems with S = -2 of light nuclei [1, 2].
So there is reason to believe that one can produce S = -2 di-baryon systems with still higher binding energies and densities using antiproton annihilation at rest.
In this contribution we present details of experimental approaches to search for the most elementary S = -2 di-proton system using the antiproton annihilation reaction on 3He targets at rest

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the strangeness S = −2 sector of low-energy hadronic physics. A hypothetical deeply bound double-antikaon dibaryon, denoted K⁻K⁻pp, is a four-body bound state consisting of two antikaons (K⁻) and two protons (p), bound by the strongly attractive K̄N interaction and predicted to have a large binding energy and high baryonic density.

Question: Does stopped-antiproton annihilation on a ³He target produce such a deeply bound S = −2 double-antikaon dibaryon state K⁻K⁻pp via the exclusive reaction
  p̄ + ³He → K⁺ + K⁰ + (K⁻K⁻pp),
and can the existence, mass, and width of this state be experimentally established with adequate resolution and statistics by the joint use of:
 (i) missing-mass spectroscopy in the K⁺K⁰ channel (with a Λ tag), and
 (ii) invariant-mass analysis of correlated ΛΛ pairs from the decay (K⁻K⁻pp) → Λ + Λ?

Determine whether such states exist as observable resonances/bound states and whether the proposed exclusive measurement strategy suffices to identify them.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that the double-antikaon dibaryon K⁻K⁻pp remains a theoretically predicted but experimentally unconfirmed state. Proposals to search for it via antiproton annihilation on ³He (e.g., at J-PARC K1.8BR with the E15 spectrometer) and via p+p collisions through a Λ(1405) doorway have been put forward, but no definitive experimental observation has been reported.

status_evidence.title: Double antikaonic nuclear clusters in antiproton-3He annihilation at J-PARC
status_evidence.snippet: Proposal to search for K⁻K⁻pp via p̄+³He → K⁺K⁰ + K⁻K⁻pp using missing-mass and ΛΛ invariant-mass analysis at J-PARC.
status_evidence.claim: The experimental search is proposed but not yet completed/confirmed.

status_evidence.title: New way to produce dense double-antikaonic dibaryon K̄K̄NN through Λ(1405)-doorway sticking in p+p collisions
status_evidence.snippet: Theoretical proposal for production of dense double-antikaonic dibaryon K̄K̄NN.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical predictions for K̄K̄NN production exist but no confirmed observation.
